summary.headline: HPL Electric Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35% YoY to ₹515 cr, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.26% on raw-material inflation, with metering margins roughly halved.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 35% YoY to ₹515 cr, the highest-ever Q1, while EIA grew 9% to ₹63 cr and PAT rose to ₹19 cr. Consumer & Industrial (C&I) hit a record ₹278 cr (+55% YoY, ~54% of revenue) and Metering & Systems grew ~17% to ₹234 cr. EBITDA margin moderated to 12.26% as metals, industrial plastics and semiconductors inflated after February 2026 due to West Asia geopolitical disruption, and depreciation from recent capacity investments weighed on PAT. Management guided that pricing and mix actions are under way, with margin recovery expected over one to three quarters if input costs ease.

segments.name: Consumer & Industrial (C&I)
segments.commentary: Record ₹278 cr revenue, +55% YoY, ~54% of Q1 revenue. Wire & cable ₹146 cr (+79%) already above 40% of FY26 full-year wire & cable revenue; lighting +78%; industrial switchgear ₹56 cr (+19%).

segments.name: Metering & Systems (smart metering)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹234 cr, ~+17% YoY. Order book ~₹3,200 cr as of 7 Aug 2026, with metering & systems over 96% of orders. Metering margin fell roughly 50% in Q1 per management, driven by industrial plastics and metals.

guidance_outlook: Management expects C&I and smart metering to both deliver revenue growth; C&I visibility of 12-18 months described as strong, with high double-digit growth expected.

Current margin levels described as a conservative baseline; recovery could take an extra quarter, with C&I margins possibly back to target by Q3 FY27 if copper and other input prices stay at current levels.
If the Middle East situation eases and crude falls, management said margins of 16-17% could be restored, and it aims to grow margins further.
Smart metering visibility of 2-3 years cited; pace depends on AMISP execution. About 7 crore meters installed nationally to date.

Capex expected to be mainly maintenance (tools, dies) for metering; new projects may need capex but are expected to carry separate revenue streams. Analyst suggested ₹50-100 cr for the next year or two; management did not confirm.
capex_capacity: Metering capacity is in place after recent investments; future metering capex is mainly maintenance (tools and dies).
Automation: recently commissioned a new MCB machine that replaces 44 workers, producing ~18,000 MCBs a day, with 7-8 such machines installed across factories. Stated ROI is 3-4 years.
Seven factories, three tool rooms and over 100 injection moulding machines; electronics manufacturing described as large and internally integrated.
Backward integration in metering: relays and some critical components are not yet made in-house; management said work is in progress under a Chinese-partner MoU but gave no timeline.
Water meters launched; gas metering considered as a future category, with no commitment.
demand_pricing: Smart metering: ~7 crore meters installed nationally per latest official figure, against a first-phase target of 25 crore. Management said the Adani group's acquisition of Intellis Smart is positive, as HPL is an approved vendor for both companies.

Smart meter pricing: contracts are fixed-price; semiconductor lead times up to 52 weeks. Management expects to pass on some price increases on new tenders, but acknowledged competitive pressure from AMISPs.
C&I pricing: wire & cable has had a couple of price increases, passed on quickly; lighting saw its first price increase in ~7-8 years; switchgear pass-through is slower.
Distribution: 900+ authorised dealers and 85,000+ retailers; 'one consumer one family' scheme incentivises cross-selling.
Data centre cables: HPL does not have the full range yet; it plans to launch products with international certifications around May-June 2027.
Exports: a Middle East utility recently approved HPL's meter; DEKRA-certified MCB and lab support sales in ~55 countries.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margins fell from ~38% to ~30%. What steps are being taken to restore margins, and is hedging used?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall mainly to input costs rising from February due to West Asia conflict. Long-term contracts, alternate materials and design changes, and price pass-through are being used; semiconductors are bought at order time, while metals and plastics cannot be hedged. Metering margins fell about 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Will smart meter price increases pass through on new tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is asking AMISPs for price increases on new orders, but competition limits this. Pricing power depends on being a trusted, quality-focused supplier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the wire & cable growth sustainable, and what is being done in channel expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Copper tonnage is up 1.5-2x from a year ago, with growth across solar, industrial, real estate and retail. Management is spending on BTS marketing, a third-party last-mile sales team and dealer/retailer expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How is the AMISP consolidation (Adani/Intellis) affecting order flow, and is there an industry tender slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the Intellis acquisition positive as HPL is approved by both. Orders are placed on 3-4 month requirements, not multi-year locks. Management said ~25 crore meters' first phase is largely tendered and enough orders exist for the next 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin baseline for new orders, and when do C&I margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Current Q1 margins are a conservative baseline; new metering orders have supply lead times of several months, so price relief comes with a lag. C&I margins could recover by Q3 FY27 if input prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex rise, and what new products are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Metering capex is mainly maintenance. New projects would carry separate revenue streams, and details will come later. Analyst's ₹50-100 cr estimate was not confirmed.

risks_watch: Metering margin pressure: management said metering margins fell roughly 50% in Q1 on industrial plastics and metals, and new orders carry supply lead times, so price relief lags.
Pricing pass-through on smart meter tenders depends on competitive AMISP negotiations; management said price increases are being requested but not secured.
Semiconductor lead times of up to 52 weeks and metals/plastics that cannot be hedged keep input-cost exposure open, with West Asia developments outside management control.
AMISP consolidation (Adani acquiring Intellis Smart, and reported interest in a meter OEM) could shift order flow; management did not comment on the second item.

Execution pace of smart meter orders depends on AMISPs; management gave no firm quarterly order inflow or tender timing, and the ~₹3,200 cr order book is said to be stable at around ₹3,000 cr over recent quarters.

Depreciation from recent capacity investments and higher manpower costs (Haryana minimum wage up ~40% in May) continue to weigh on profit conversion; relay and critical metering components are not yet made in-house with no timeline given.

summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth in C&I and smart metering, with a cautious tone on margins: management repeatedly tied recovery to geopolitical easing, crude and copper prices, and pricing actions with time lags. It declined to give numbers on AMISP tender flow, the Adani-related OEM news, backward-integration timelines and capex size.
